turns.replyText:
Is a damaged item handled differently from a normal return?

Yes, a damaged item is handled differently than a normal return, especially for plants.

1. Live plants (roses, perennials, bulbs)

We do not take live plants back as returns.
If something arrives damaged or you have concerns about its condition, our garden advisors review your photos and details and then decide next steps under our guarantee.
So instead of a “send it back” type return, it is treated as a damage/quality concern and evaluated for possible warranty coverage.

2. Non-plant items (tools, markers, supplies)

Tools and most hard goods can be returned within 30 days if they are unused and in new condition; you’d ship them back and, if approved, receive a refund to your original payment method.
Custom-engraved Garden Markers are not returnable unless there is an issue with the engraving.
If a non-plant item arrives damaged or defective, you’d still contact us with photos, and the team would review that a bit differently than a simple “changed my mind” return.

If you’d like help with your specific damaged item, reply with:

Your email address
Your order number (or your full name and shipping address if you don’t have the number handy)
The name of the damaged item
Photos of the damage and the box/label

Then the team can review your situation and follow up with next steps.

turns.replyText:
Will I get a replacement or a refund?

I hear you wanting to know what will actually happen, and that makes total sense.

For any damaged item, our team reviews the photos and details first, then decides what’s appropriate in your specific case. I can’t promise a replacement or a refund, because that decision belongs to our garden advisors.

Here’s how it generally works:

Plants (roses, perennials, bulbs):
These are covered under our guarantee. If a claim is approved, you receive store credit to use on our website, not a refund back to your original payment method and not an automatic replacement. The advisors look at your photos and information and then let you know the outcome and details of any credit.

Non-plant items (tools, markers, other products):
Damaged or defective non-plant items are also reviewed by the team. They’ll look at your photos and order details and then follow up with the next steps for that item.

If you haven’t already, the best next step is to send:

Your email address
Your order number (or your full name and shipping address if you don’t have the number handy)
The name of the damaged item
Photos of the damage, the outside of the box, and the shipping label

You can share those details and photos here in chat or email them to info@heirloomroses.com. Once they have everything, the team will review your situation and then reach out to you with what they can offer.
